claims.text: A 5–10 at.% Al addition combined with optimized homogenization and controlled pre-oxidation promotes uniformly dispersed, coherent submicron Al2O3 precipitates in AlxFeCoNiCr alloys.
The proposed Al2O3 precipitates reduce the alloy density.
The proposed Al2O3 precipitates strengthen the matrix through dislocation pinning.
The proposed Al2O3 precipitates improve corrosion resistance by supporting a continuous protective oxide scale.
The proposed Al2O3 precipitates improve high-temperature oxidation resistance by supporting a continuous protective oxide scale.
The baseline alloy contains less than 1 at.% Al, whereas the modified alloy contains 5–10 at.% Al.
Optimized homogenization and pre-oxidation stabilize Al2O3 precipitates at subgrain boundaries and within the matrix.
At high temperature, added Al preferentially oxidizes in situ to form a coherent network of Al2O3 precipitates.
The lower atomic mass of Al relative to the principal alloying elements reduces the modified alloy's overall density.
The modified alloy will have lower density than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will have higher yield strength and tensile strength than the baseline alloy because of nanoprecipitate strengthening.
The modified alloy will have better resistance to corrosion in 0.5 M NaCl than the baseline alloy.
The modified alloy will oxidize more slowly and form a more stable, coherent oxide scale at approximately 800°C in air than the baseline alloy.
An AlxFeCoNiCr alloy containing less than 1 at.% Al does not promote controlled formation of Al2O3 precipitates.
Precipitate coarsening or inhomogeneity during service would negate the expected mechanical and environmental-property improvements.
Precipitation strengthening and protective oxide-scale formation are well-established mechanisms.
